newsitem.title: USA: Union weighs organizing Conn. casinos - paper.
newsitem.headline: Union weighs organizing Conn. casinos - paper.

text.p: A national union that represents gambling workers said it was deciding how much effort to invest in a drive to unionize Connecticut's Native American casinos, the Hartford Courant said on Friday.

The union has been been meeting on and off with casino employees for several years, and a recent survey led the union, Local 217 of the Hotel and Restaurant Employees, to believe the time was ripe for a campaign.

The poll found workers were most concerned about their lack of control or involvement in decisions that affect their wages, schedules and working conditions, the paper said. Local 217 falls under the umbrella of the AFL-CIO federation of unions.

The Foxwoods and Mohegan Sun casinos have about 15,000 workers. An official from Foxwoods, where the drive was expected to start, told the paper it believed that its grievance procedures were more than adequate. Officials at the Mohegan Sun declined to comment.

State and federal laws designed to guarantee safety, fair wages and equal treatment in the workplace do not necessarily apply to the casinos because they are on sovereign Native American land, the paper said.
A union official said it would not try to work within the parameters of the National Labor Relations Act, but instead define the drive along the lines of a human rights campaign.
